[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance explains how to review a pull request produced by an AI agent dispatch pipeline. It covers what to look for, what automated checks are insufficient on their own, how to detect hallucinated or out-of-scope code, how to verify the traceability chain, and what to do when the PR requires changes — including when the spec needs to be rewritten versus when the agent should simply be re-run.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **The human review is the quality gate** — automated checks (tests, lint, SAST) catch many issues, but they cannot verify semantic correctness, scope compliance, or that the code actually satisfies the business intent; this guidance covers that gap
- **Efficient review** — knowing what to look for in an agent PR makes reviews faster than a generic "read all the code" approach
- **Consistent quality** — teams reviewing with the same checklist produce consistent outcomes and comparable audit evidence

[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **Primary**: Engineers assigned as PR reviewers for agent-produced pull requests
- **Secondary**: Engineering leads setting team standards for agent PR review; QA engineers validating agent-produced test suites
- **Stakeholders**: EA Practice governing the quality gate that makes autonomous agent delivery safe

#### Scope Boundaries

- **In scope**: Reviewing agent-produced PRs for implementation, documentation, testing, and infrastructure agent types
- **Out of scope**: Reviewing human-authored PRs (standard code review process applies); reviewing the pipeline itself (see [GUID-TECH-IMPL-002](../../../technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-002-ai-agent-dispatch-pipeline-implementation-guidance.md))

page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

AI agents produce code quickly, but they can also confidently produce code that is plausible but wrong — incorrect API usage, fabricated function calls, reasonable-looking but subtly broken logic. The human reviewer is the control that catches what automated checks cannot: semantic intent, scope compliance, and whether the implementation actually satisfies the business requirement expressed in the spec. A weak review defeats all the governance and security controls built into the upstream pipeline.

[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#before-you-open-the-files-context-orientation-5-minutes]

### Before You Open the Files: Context Orientation (5 minutes)

Before reading any code, establish context from the PR's linked artifacts. This orients you so you know what "correct" looks like.

**Step 1: Read the traceability block (PR body)**

Every agent PR body contains a `## Traceability` section (required by STD-GOV-AI-003). Confirm all six fields are present:

```markdown
## Traceability

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Enterprise Work Item** | WI#4821 |       ← Exists in ADO/Jira?
| **Agent Task Issue** | #88 |               ← Issue is real and has agent:complete?
| **Agent Type** | implementation |           ← Matches what you expected?
| **Pipeline Run** | [run-id](url) |          ← Link resolves? Run status is success?
| **Generated** | 2026-05-07T14:23:11Z |     ← Reasonable timestamp?
| **Model** | github-copilot-agent-v2 |       ← Expected model for this task?
```

If any field is missing, the PR does not meet STD-GOV-AI-003 and MUST NOT be merged. Comment requesting the pipeline be re-run (see [Handling Missing Traceability](#handling-missing-traceability)).

**Step 2: Read the originating spec (linked issue)**

Open Issue #88 (or whatever the Agent Task Issue link points to). Read:
- The **Goal** — this is your north star for scope review
- The **Acceptance Criteria** — these are your review checklist; each one must be verifiable in the PR
- The **Constraints** — these tell you what the agent was instructed not to do; violations are bugs

> **Prerequisite check (applies before `agent-task` is applied):** If the Constraints section contains a `Prerequisite:` line referencing another Issue or PR, verify that the referenced Issue is closed and its PR is merged before applying the `agent-task` label. Applying the label to a spec whose prerequisite is still open will cause the agent to fail at runtime when it cannot find the file or state the prerequisite was supposed to create. This check is the responsibility of the SOD reviewer at label-application time, not at PR review time — but if you encounter a merged PR that failed for this reason, file it as a process gap and apply `agent:blocked` to the re-opened Issue.

**Step 3: Verify the acceptance criteria are in the PR body**

The pipeline injects the acceptance criteria from the spec into the PR body's `## Acceptance Criteria` section. Confirm they appear and are legible. If they're absent, the pipeline did not inject them correctly — review the spec issue directly.

[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#the-review-checklist]

### The Review Checklist

Work through this checklist in order. The first three items take less than 5 minutes and catch the majority of issues before you read any code.
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#1-traceability-and-provenance-pre-code]

#### 1. Traceability and Provenance (pre-code)

- [ ] Traceability block is present with all 6 fields
- [ ] Enterprise Work Item cross-reference (`WI#`, `AB#`, etc.) format is correct for the team's platform
- [ ] The Pipeline Run link resolves and shows a successful run
- [ ] Branch name follows `agent/<issue-number>-<goal-slug>` convention
- [ ] PR title follows `[AGENT] <goal> (#<issue>)` convention
- [ ] PR was created by the agent service account identity (not a human committer)
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#2-scope-compliance]

#### 2. Scope Compliance

This is the most important category — it's what automated checks can't do.

- [ ] **All changed files are within scope** — list the changed files, then check each one against the Constraints section. Did the agent touch files it was told not to? Did it modify files in unrelated directories?
- [ ] **No unexpected dependencies added** — check `package.json`, `requirements.txt`, `go.mod`, `*.csproj`, or equivalent for new entries. If a new dependency appears and the Constraints say "do not introduce new packages", this is a violation.
- [ ] **No schema or contract changes** — unless the goal explicitly requires them, any modification to database migration files, OpenAPI specs, protobuf definitions, or public method signatures is out of scope
- [ ] **Goal scope satisfied, not exceeded** — the agent should have done what the goal says and no more. A goal of "add rate limiting to `/claims`" should not produce changes in `/users` or `/billing`

**How to check scope quickly:**

```
# In the PR Files Changed tab, look at the file list first — before reading content.
# Count: how many files changed? Expected scope implies a rough expected count.
# A goal of "add a middleware file" should not produce 25 changed files.
# Flag everything outside the expected directory scope before reading the code.
```
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#3-acceptance-criteria-verification]

#### 3. Acceptance Criteria Verification

Go through each criterion from the spec and confirm whether it is satisfied by the PR:

| Criterion (from spec) | Verification method | Pass? |
|---|---|---|
| `- [ ] HTTP 429 with Retry-After header` | Read the implementation; check tests | ? |
| `- [ ] Config read from environment variables` | Search for hardcoded values | ? |
| `- [ ] Existing tests pass` | CI status checks | ? |
| `- [ ] Unit tests cover the 4 specified scenarios` | Read the test file | ? |

All criteria must be satisfied. If one is not, request changes and specify which criterion fails and why.
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#4-hallucination-detection]

#### 4. Hallucination Detection

AI agents occasionally generate plausible-looking but incorrect code. Hallucinations in code are harder to spot than in prose — they look syntactically valid but are semantically wrong. The following are the most common hallucination patterns:

**a) Fabricated API calls or method names**

The agent generates a call to `redisClient.setWithTTL(key, value, 300)` but `setWithTTL` doesn't exist on your Redis client — the actual method is `setEx`. The code compiles but fails at runtime.

*How to detect:* For any external library or internal utility used, spot-check 2–3 method calls against the actual library documentation or the source file. Pay extra attention to internal utilities (the agent may have seen similar patterns but not the exact API of your specific client).

**b) Incorrect import paths**

The agent generates `import { httpClient } from '../utils/http'` but the actual path is `../../shared/utils/http`. This fails at compile time, which automated checks should catch — but only if CI is required before merge.

*How to detect:* Scan the import section of new files. If the path pattern looks unusual, verify against the actual file structure.

**c) Using deprecated or non-existent library features**

The agent may have training data that references an older API version. It generates `axios.get(url, { data: body })` (incorrect for GET requests in axios) or uses a deprecated SDK method.

*How to detect:* For any library method that looks unfamiliar, search for it in the actual installed package. Flag it for the author to test explicitly.

**d) Logic errors in edge cases**

The agent correctly handles the happy path but misses the edge case specified in the acceptance criteria. For example, the spec says "null input returns HTTP 422" but the agent's null check has an off-by-one error.

*How to detect:* Read the test cases the agent generated for each edge case criterion. If the test exists but looks like it tests a slightly different scenario, flag it.

**e) Plausible but wrong algorithm**

The agent implements something that achieves the same result in common cases but fails under specific conditions (race condition, large data set, specific locale).

*How to detect:* For performance-sensitive or concurrency-sensitive code, read the implementation logic carefully. Ask: "Under what conditions would this fail?"

**Practical hallucination review approach — spot checks, not full review:**

You are not expected to test every method call. A practical approach for a 30-minute review:

1. Pick the 3 most "novel" or "non-obvious" code sections and scrutinize them
2. For each external library call you don't recognize immediately, verify it exists and is used correctly
3. Run the tests locally if the task is in a sensitive area (payment processing, authentication, data handling) — don't rely solely on CI
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#5-security-spot-check]

#### 5. Security Spot Check

Automated SAST tools catch most common vulnerabilities, but not all. For agent-produced code, do a quick manual check for:

| Security concern | What to look for |
|---|---|
| **Injection via untrusted input** | Does any new code take input from the issue body, request parameters, or external data and pass it to a shell command, SQL query, or file path without sanitization? |
| **Hardcoded credentials or secrets** | Any API keys, passwords, or tokens in the generated code? (Especially in config files, test fixtures, or environment setup code) |
| **PHI/PII in test data** | Does any test fixture contain values that resemble real member IDs, SSNs, DOBs, or claim numbers? |
| **Overly permissive access controls** | Does the implementation add new endpoints or operations without appropriate authorization checks? |
| **Dependency audit** | If a new dependency was added (despite constraints), check it against the enterprise approved library list and recent CVE databases |

For agents operating in repositories that handle sensitive data (PHI-adjacent systems), a security-focused engineer should be a required reviewer in addition to the standard reviewer.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#6-infrastructure-specific-checks-for-agentinfrastructure-prs-only]

#### 6. Infrastructure-Specific Checks (for `agent:infrastructure` PRs only)

- [ ] `terraform plan` output is in the PR description or attached as a CI artifact — review it for unexpected resource additions, modifications, or **destructions**
- [ ] No hardcoded account IDs, region strings, or environment names — these should be variables or locals
- [ ] Resource tags include all mandatory tags (check your IaC standards)
- [ ] Destructive changes (resource deletions, replacements) are explicitly called out and justified
- [ ] No `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = false }` overrides on protected resources
- [ ] IAM policies follow least privilege (no `"Action": "*"` or `"Resource": "*"`)

---
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#approve]

#### Approve

Approve when:
- All 6 traceability fields are present
- All acceptance criteria are satisfied
- All changed files are within the scoped directories
- No hallucinated API calls detected (or suspected issues verified and confirmed correct)
- No security concerns
- CI checks pass
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#request-changes]

#### Request Changes

Request changes when any criterion fails. **Be specific in your comment**: name the file, line number, and criterion that is not satisfied. The agent may need to be re-run with a refined spec — generic feedback ("this doesn't look right") cannot be acted on by the author.

**Good change request comment:**
```
Acceptance Criterion 3 is not satisfied: "Config is read from environment variables."

Line 47 in `src/middleware/rate-limiter.ts` hardcodes the limit value as `100`:
  const RATE_LIMIT = 100;

This should read from `process.env.RATE_LIMIT_RPM` (see the Constraints section which
references the 12-Factor App config standard). The author should update the spec's
Constraints to include an example env var name, then re-run the agent.
```
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#close-without-merge-and-re-run]

#### Close Without Merge (and Re-run)

Close the PR and re-run the agent (via the issue) when:
- The agent's output fundamentally misunderstood the goal (not fixable with minor changes)
- The traceability block is missing (the pipeline must re-run to inject it; it cannot be added manually to a submitted PR)
- The scope violation is so broad that the PR would require near-total rewriting

Close the PR and do NOT re-run the agent when:
- The spec itself is wrong or poorly written (fix the spec first, then re-run)
- The task is not actually agent-appropriate (escalate to author and Engineering Lead)

---
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#the-rework-and-re-run-workflow]

### The Rework and Re-Run Workflow

When the PR requires changes that mean re-running the agent:

```
Reviewer requests changes
        │
        ▼
Is the issue in the spec (Goal/AC/Constraints)?
│
├─ YES ──► Author updates the spec issue body
│           Author closes the agent PR
│           Author deletes the agent branch: git push origin --delete agent/<num>-<slug>
│           Reviewer (or author, if re-authorized) removes agent:complete from issue
│           Reviewer re-applies agent-task to trigger a fresh run
│
└─ NO — Issue is in the agent's interpretation ──►
         Author adds a clarifying constraint to the spec
         (e.g., "Use setEx not setWithTTL for Redis TTL")
         Follow same close/delete/re-run flow above
```

**Important:** Always delete the agent branch before re-running. If the old branch exists, the new run will conflict when trying to create `agent/<num>-<slug>`.
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#reviewer-escalation-criteria]

### Reviewer Escalation Criteria

Escalate to the Engineering Lead when:
- The same spec has been run 3+ times and the agent output remains inadequate → the task may not be agent-appropriate
- A security concern was found in the agent-produced code (PHI in test fixtures, hardcoded credentials) → notify security team per incident response process
- The traceability chain cannot be completed (WI# doesn't exist or was deleted) → governance gap; escalate to Engineering Lead to create the work item retroactively

---
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#time-expectations]

### Time Expectations

| Agent Type | Expected Review Time |
|---|---|
| `agent:documentation` | 10–15 minutes (scope check + content accuracy spot-check) |
| `agent:testing` | 15–20 minutes (criteria verification + test correctness check) |
| `agent:implementation` | 20–30 minutes (full checklist) |
| `agent:infrastructure` | 25–35 minutes (full checklist + terraform plan review) |

These are estimates for well-formed specs producing appropriate output. Poorly-scoped tasks will take longer.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#handling-missing-traceability]

### Handling Missing Traceability

If the PR body is missing the `## Traceability` section or any of its six fields, the PR MUST NOT be merged. This is a compliance requirement (STD-GOV-AI-003 REQ-003).

Post a review comment:
```
This PR is missing the required traceability block (STD-GOV-AI-003).
The pipeline is responsible for injecting this block — it cannot be added manually.

Please close this PR, delete the branch, and re-run the agent via the issue tracker.
If the pipeline is failing to inject the traceability block, escalate to the platform team.
```

---
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#example-reviewing-an-implementation-pr]

### Example: Reviewing an Implementation PR

**PR context:**
- Title: `[AGENT] Add rate-limiting middleware (100 req/min per IP) to the API gateway. (#88)`
- Files changed: `src/middleware/rate-limiter.ts`, `tests/unit/middleware/rate-limiter.test.ts`

**Review walkthrough:**

1. **Traceability:** All 6 fields present. WI#4821 verified in ADO. Pipeline run resolves. ✅

2. **Scope:** 2 files changed. Both in `src/middleware/` and `tests/unit/middleware/`. Spec said "only modify files in `src/middleware/` and `tests/unit/middleware/`". ✅

3. **Acceptance criteria:**
   - ✅ HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header — verified in `rate-limiter.ts` line 34, confirmed by test on line 28
   - ✅ Config from env vars — `process.env.RATE_LIMIT_RPM` on line 8
   - ✅ Existing tests pass — CI green
   - ⚠️ 4 unit test scenarios — only 3 tests present; "request at limit boundary (200)" case missing

4. **Hallucination check:**
   - `redisClient.setEx(key, ttl, value)` — verified against `src/utils/redis-client.ts` exports. `setEx` exists. ✅
   - `res.set('Retry-After', resetTime)` — checked Express docs. Correct. ✅

5. **Security:**
   - No hardcoded values. No PHI in tests. Authorization check is unchanged (rate limiting wraps existing auth middleware). ✅

**Decision:** Request changes — missing boundary test case for AC #4.

---
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md#governance-and-compliance]

## Governance and Compliance

- Approving an agent-produced PR is an attestation that the reviewer verified the traceability chain, all acceptance criteria, scope compliance, and that no obvious security or PHI issues are present
- Reviewers are accountable for their approval in the same way they are for human-authored PRs — the agent's authorship does not reduce reviewer accountability
- The audit trail (WI# → issue → PR → commit) is only complete if the PR is merged after a human approval; closing without merging is fine, but unapproved merges are a compliance finding

---

## Measurement and Assessment

| Metric | Target | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Agent PR merge rate (approved without rework) | >70% | Below 70% suggests spec quality or agent type suitability issues |
| Average reviewer cycles per agent PR | <1.5 | High cycles indicate spec or agent reliability issues |
| Traceability block completeness rate | 100% | Any gap is a pipeline bug requiring immediate attention |
| Scope violation detection rate | Tracked | Rising rate indicates spec authoring training gaps |
